transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I... honestly, I only came in today because my husband wouldn't stop nagging me about it, making it this whole big deal. Him and the people down at the warehouse where I work—I move freight, you know, loading and unloading heavy pallets all shift—they all keep acting like I'm crazy. Like I'm the one with the problem or I'm making things up in my head. But I'm not stupid. I might not have finished high school, but I know how to do my job, and I know exactly what I see. 

I know for an absolute fact that they have been watching my moves. Every single thing I do on that floor, they're tracking it. I'll be down in the loading bay, right? And I'll stack a pallet, count the boxes, wrap it up tight, and log it. And then... the numbers in the system just magically change. Somebody is going in and changing my pallet counts behind my back. It’s like, I turn around for two seconds to grab the pallet jack, and bam, my count is suddenly short or the manifest is wrong. They’re doing it on purpose to sabotage me. There’s a day-shift supervisor spot opening up, and they are doing everything they possibly can to keep me from getting it. They want me to look like I can't even count my own freight so they can give the job to someone else. And when I try to explain this to my husband, he just takes their side! He looks at me like I'm losing it and tells me I need to go see a doctor. So here I am, just to get him off my back. But I'm telling you, I'm not the one with the problem here, they're the ones messing with my numbers and watching me from the catwalks...
Do you think someone is intentionally trying to harm you or your reputation at work?

Well, yeah, exactly! Like I was just saying, that is exactly what they are doing. It’s not just some accident or a glitch in the scanner system, you know? They are absolutely trying to ruin my reputation on the floor. Because, think about it... if the shift manager comes down to the dock and sees my log sheet doesn't match the actual freight sitting right there on the skid, who looks stupid? I do. I look like I can't even do basic math, like I'm some kind of idiot who can't count to fifty. 

And I know how to count! I've been doing this for years. But they want management to think I'm completely incompetent so I don't get that day-shift supervisor spot. I know they're watching me, waiting for their chance. I can literally feel it. I'll be wrapping a pallet with the shrink wrap, you know, going around and around, pulling it tight, and I’ll look up at the metal catwalks above the loading bay and I just... I know someone is up there. They hide up there in the shadows, just waiting for me to go on my fifteen-minute break or run to the bathroom so they can sneak down and mess with my scanner or change the numbers I already put in the computer. It is one hundred percent deliberate. 

And the worst part—the absolute worst part of all of this—is that when I try to defend myself, when I tell my husband that these people are literally plotting against me to keep me at the bottom, he just sighs. He gives me this... this *look*. Like I'm the one losing my grip. That is the whole reason I'm even sitting in this chair talking to you right now, because he and the guys at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy for just pointing out the obvious truth. They’re making *me* out to be the crazy one when they are the ones sneaking around changing my pallet counts! It's not fair, it really isn't, because I work hard, I sweat out there on that concrete for ten, twelve hours a day, and for them to just try and sabotage my whole livelihood and then call me crazy on top of it... I mean, wouldn't you be upset? It's just... it's a whole conspiracy against me, and nobody wants to listen to the facts.
Do you think these people are targeting you specifically for a reason, or is it just because of the job promotion?

Well, it’s… it’s definitely the promotion, but it’s more than just that. It’s like… they know I’m the only one who actually does the work right, you know? They know I’m better than them. I mean, I’m out there sweating, lifting, stacking, making sure every single pallet is wrapped so tight it could survive a hurricane, and they’re just… they’re threatened by me. So yeah, it’s the supervisor spot, but it’s also just… me. They’re targeting *me*. 

And like I said, I only even came in here today because my husband and the people at the warehouse just won't let it go. They keep acting like I’m the one who’s crazy, like I’m making this all up in my head! But I know what I see. I know they have been watching my moves from the catwalks. I know they are sneaking around and changing my pallet counts in the computer system just to make me look incompetent. It’s a deliberate plan to keep me from getting that supervisor spot, and they think if they just call me crazy enough times, I’ll start to believe it. Or my husband will believe it, which he already is doing, by the way. He just takes their side and tells me I need help. But I don't need help, I need them to stop messing with my numbers! I mean, if you were in my shoes, and you knew for a fact that people were sabotaging your work and then gaslighting you about it, wouldn't you be furious? It’s just so obvious what they’re doing, and nobody will just listen to me and look at the facts!
Do you feel like you have special abilities or qualities that set you apart from others at the warehouse?

Special abilities? I mean, I don't know if I'd call it a "special ability," like I'm some kind of superhero or something... I'm not saying I have magic powers. But... I do know that I am the hardest worker on that floor. Period. No one else out there can stack a pallet like I can. I mean, you have to know how to distribute the weight, right? You can't just throw heavy boxes of auto parts on top of fragile stuff. You have to build a solid foundation, interlock the boxes like bricks, wrap it from the bottom up, nice and tight so it doesn't shift in transit. I do it perfectly every single time. 

So, it's not a special power, it's just that I'm actually competent, unlike the rest of them who just stand around leaning on their pallet jacks, waiting for the clock to run out. They see how fast I move, how much freight I clear in a shift, and they know they can't keep up. That's why they have to cheat. That's why they have to sneak into the system and mess with my numbers, because if we were just going off raw talent and hard work, I'd have had that supervisor job months ago. So no, no "special abilities" or whatever you want to call it... I just know how to do my job better than anyone else in that entire warehouse, and they hate me for it.
Do you think these people watching you and changing your pallet counts are part of a larger plan against you, or is it just about the job at the warehouse?

Well, like I keep saying... I don't know about some giant, you know, worldwide government thing or whatever, if that's what you're asking. It's about the warehouse. But it feels like this huge, massive plan against me because everyone is in on it. I mean, I feel like a broken record here, but it's the whole reason I even walked through your door today. I only came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse just will not stop acting like I'm crazy! It's like they've all teamed up. 

They treat me like I've completely lost my mind, but I know exactly what I'm seeing. I know they have been watching my moves every single shift. I'm not stupid. I see the shadows, I know they're up there, and I know they are changing the pallet counts the second I step away from my station. And it all comes back to that supervisor spot. That is what this is all about. They want to keep me from getting it, so they mess with my freight numbers, and then when I call them out on it, they just... they flip it around on me! They tell my husband I'm acting paranoid or whatever, and he actually buys it. He just takes their side. 

So, yeah, it's about the job, but the way they're going about it—sneaking around, ruining my hard work, turning my own husband against me so he thinks I need to be sitting in a doctor's office—it's just... it's a completely orchestrated plan to ruin me. And it is incredibly frustrating that I'm the only one who sees it for what it actually is.
Do you still believe people are watching you and sabotaging your work when you're not at the warehouse?

Well, when I'm not at the warehouse... I mean, I don't know. I don't think they're following me to the grocery store or anything like that. It's not like I see them peeking through my windows at home. But the thing is, the sabotage doesn't just stop when I punch out, you know? Because even when I'm sitting on my couch, trying to watch TV or just eat dinner with my husband, the damage is already done. They've already messed with the system. They've already planted those seeds of doubt in my husband's head. 

So, are they physically watching me at home? No, I don't think so. But it feels like they're still there, if that makes sense. Because I'm sitting there, and I can't even relax. I'm just running through the whole shift in my head, trying to remember exactly how many pallets I wrapped, trying to figure out exactly when they logged in and changed my numbers. And then my husband will look at me with that... that *look*, you know? That pitying look, like I'm a fragile little bird who's lost her mind. And I know it's because of them. I know they've been talking to him, or he's been talking to them, and they're just feeding him all these lies about how I'm acting erratic or whatever word they use. 

So even when I'm miles away from that warehouse, they're still ruining my life. They're still sabotaging me, just in a different way. It's like I can't escape it. I go to work, I get watched and cheated. I go home, I get treated like a psychiatric patient by the man who's supposed to have my back. It's exhausting. It really is. I just want to do my job, do it well, and get the promotion I deserve. Is that really so much to ask? But no, they have to make it this whole big thing, and it just bleeds into every single part of my life, even when I'm nowhere near a pallet jack.
Do you think people are still watching you or plotting against you when you're not thinking about work or the warehouse?

Well, that's the thing, isn't it? It's like I was just saying... I can't really *not* think about work. It's not like I have a switch in my brain where I can just turn off the warehouse and go, "Oh, time to relax and think about the weather." Because even if I try, even if I sit down and try to watch a movie or something, it always comes back to it. Because... I mean, I wouldn't even be here, sitting in this chair, talking to you, if it wasn't for them. 

I literally only came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse just will not let it go. They keep acting like I'm completely crazy, like I'm the one who's losing it. But I'm not! I know what I'm seeing. I know they have been watching my every move up there on the catwalks, and I know for a fact they are changing my pallet counts. It's so obvious what they're doing. They know I'm the fastest, they know I'm the most efficient, and they are terrified I'm going to get that supervisor spot. That's what this whole thing is about. 

So even when I'm not physically there, even if I try to just put it out of my mind, how can I? My husband is sitting right there, looking at me like I'm a mental patient, because they got to him. They convinced him that I'm just making this all up. So no, I don't think they're hiding in my bushes or following my car, but the plot, the whole plan to ruin me and keep me from getting that promotion... it's always there. It's happening whether I'm thinking about it or not, because the damage is already done, you know? They've already turned my own house into a place where I have to defend my sanity.
Do you feel like you're being watched or sabotaged when you're with friends or family outside of work?

Look, Doc, I feel like we're just going in circles here. I mean... family? Friends? Outside of work? It all just comes back to the exact same thing I've been telling you since I first sat down in this chair. I don't have some, like, secret agent following me to a family barbecue or anything like that. That's not what's happening. But the sabotage? Yeah, it's always there, just hanging over me, because of what they've done to my life. 

Like I keep saying—and I know I sound like a total broken record right now, I really do—but I literally only came in here today because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy. That's the whole reason! I go over to my sister's house, or I'm just trying to have a normal Sunday with my husband, and they all have this... this attitude, you know? Like they're handling a ticking time bomb. Because the people at work got into my husband's head, and now he talks to the rest of the family, and suddenly everyone is looking at me sideways, whispering when I leave the room or asking me if I'm feeling okay in that fake, sweet voice. 

But I know what's real. I know for an absolute fact they have been watching my every single move up there on the floor. I know they are changing the pallet counts in the system. And it is one hundred percent to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. 

So, no, my friends aren't the ones changing my freight numbers, obviously. But the whole situation just bleeds into everything else. My husband thinks I'm losing it, my family treats me like I'm delicate, and it's all because those guys at the warehouse are terrified I'm going to be their boss and they're pulling all these strings to stop it. It's just... it's exhausting having to explain this over and over. Do you get what I'm saying? It's all connected to the warehouse, but it ruins my time with my family anyway because they've turned everyone against me.
Do you think the people watching you and sabotaging your work are only doing it at the warehouse, or are they involved in other parts of your life as well?

Doc, I... I really don't know how many different ways I can say the exact same thing to you. We are literally just going over and over this. Are they physically involved in other parts of my life? No. Like I just said two minutes ago, they aren't hiding in my grocery cart or sitting at my dining room table. They don't *need* to be. 

Because, like I told you, I only came in here today because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy. They've convinced him! So yeah, they are involved in my home life because they poisoned it by getting in his head. But the actual watching? The actual sabotage? That is happening at the warehouse. I know they have been watching my moves up there on the floor. I know they are changing the pallet counts. It's a fact. I log my numbers, I wrap the freight, I know exactly what I pull every single shift. I'm the fastest one there. And then the numbers in the computer just magically drop by the end of the week? Come on. 

It's all because of the supervisor spot. That's the whole point of all of this. They want to keep me from getting that supervisor spot, and they don't care who they have to drag into it—my husband, my family, whoever—to make me look like I'm losing my mind so management won't promote me. So they don't need to follow me around after I clock out. They just need to make everyone at home think I'm the one with the problem, which is exactly what they did, and that's why I'm stuck in this office having to defend myself right now.
Do you think the people sabotaging you at work are also affecting other parts of your life outside of work?

Doc, seriously... are you messing with me right now? Is this some kind of psychological test where you just ask the exact same question five times in a row to see if I finally snap? Because I swear, I feel like I'm talking to a brick wall here. I am sitting here, trying to make you understand my reality, and you just keep repeating yourself! 

Yes! Yes, it affects other parts of my life! I literally just spent the last ten minutes explaining exactly how it bleeds into my home life! Look, let me just spell it out one more time, from the very top, okay? Please, just listen to me this time. 

I only came in here today because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy. That is the entire reason I am sitting in this room with you. They got into my husband's head, so now my marriage is completely stressed out, my home life feels like an interrogation, and everyone is treating me like a headcase. But I am not! I know exactly what I'm talking about. I know they have been watching my moves up there on the floor. I know they are going into the system and changing the pallet counts on my shifts. I build those pallets, I wrap them, I load them—I know my numbers! 

And they are doing all of this, they are going to all this trouble to make me look incompetent and crazy, just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. That's it. That's the whole thing. So yes, what they do at the warehouse affects my life outside of work, because they've made my own husband think I'm insane just to protect their own jobs. Do you finally see what I'm saying? Please tell me you get it now, because I don't think I can explain it another way.
Do you think people are plotting against you when you're not thinking about work or the warehouse?

Okay, wow. Just... wow. I honestly don't even know what to say to you anymore, Doc. Are you even listening to the words coming out of my mouth? When am I ever *not* thinking about work or the warehouse? It's my livelihood! It's my life! You try going in every single day, busting your back, moving heavy freight, sweating through your clothes, knowing you are the absolute best worker they have on the floor, and then realizing your own coworkers are actively trying to destroy you. It consumes you! You don't just turn that off. 

So no, I don't think random people on the street are plotting against me when I'm watching TV or whatever it is you're trying to get me to say. 

Let me be as crystal clear as I possibly can, and please, write this down so you stop asking me the exact same thing. I only came in here today because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy. That is the only reason! I don't have some wild imagination where the whole entire world is out to get me. It is specifically them. Because I know they have been watching my moves. I see them looking. I know they are going into that computer and changing the pallet counts to make my numbers look bad. 

And I know exactly why they're doing it, too—to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. That spot is mine, I earned it, and they are stealing it by making my own husband think I'm losing my mind so I'll get discredited and management will pass me over. Why is this so hard for you to understand? It's not everyone everywhere, it's just them, doing this one specific thing, and I really, really need you to hear me on this so we can move on.
Do you think the people watching you and sabotaging your work are only interested in what happens at the warehouse, or do they care about other things you do?

Doc... are you... I mean, seriously, is there a hidden camera in here? Am I being pranked right now? Because I literally just answered this. I have answered this exact same question like four times in the last twenty minutes! Is there something wrong with your hearing, or is this just how psychiatrists try to wear people down? 

Let me break it down again, real slow, okay? Because I honestly don't know how else to get this through to you. 

They do not care about what I do outside of work unless it helps them ruin me at work. They don't care if I go to the grocery store, they don't care what I watch on TV, they don't care what I make for dinner. They care about the warehouse. They care about the supervisor spot. That is it! 

Look, I only came in here today because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy. They are all teaming up to act like I'm the one losing it, and my husband bought it hook, line, and sinker. But I am not crazy! I know what I see with my own two eyes. I know they have been watching my moves on the floor, clocking every single thing I do from the racks. I know they are going into the computer system and changing the pallet counts to make my productivity look like absolute garbage. I physically move that freight, Doc. I stack it, I shrink-wrap it, I load it on the dock. I know exactly what I did on my shift! 

And they are doing all of this—all this sneaking around, all this lying and messing with my numbers—just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. That is the beginning, middle, and end of the whole entire thing. They just want that promotion for themselves, so they made my husband think I'm crazy so I'd end up sitting in a doctor's office instead of in the manager's office getting the promotion I actually earned. 

Do you finally, finally understand what I am saying to you? Because I am telling you right now, I am not answering this question a fifth time. Can we please just talk about something else?
Do you think about the people watching you and sabotaging your work when you're asleep or dreaming?

Sleep? Dreaming? Are you kidding me right now? Okay, you know what, I am actually starting to think you're the one who needs to get checked out, because you are literally not hearing a single word I say. I just told you, not two minutes ago, that I wasn't going to answer this again, and here you go, asking the exact same thing but throwing the word 'dreams' in there like it makes it a brand new question! 

Look, when I actually manage to close my eyes—which is barely ever, by the way, because my body is completely aching from pulling heavy freight and wrapping pallets all day, and my brain is too stressed to shut off—no, I am not dreaming about them. I don't need to dream about them because it is happening in real life, right in front of my face, while I am wide awake! 

I feel like I'm the one going crazy just trying to talk to you. How many different ways do I have to explain my own life to you? I came in here today because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy. That is the only reason I am sitting in this chair! My husband looks at me like I'm some kind of stranger now, like I'm a ticking time bomb in my own house, because those guys at work got into his head. But I am not crazy. I know what is real. I know for a fact, one hundred percent, that they have been watching my moves on the floor. I catch them out of the corner of my eye when I'm down the aisles pulling stock. I know they are going into the computer system, logging in, and changing the pallet counts on my shifts to make my numbers look like I'm just standing around doing nothing. 

And why do they do it? I've told you this! To keep me from getting that supervisor spot! It means getting off the floor, it means I don't have to kill my knees on the concrete all day, and they want it for themselves. So they mess with my numbers and they team up to convince my husband I'm losing my grip on reality. That is what is happening. Not a dream. Real life. Now, please, for the love of God, ask me a different question before I walk right out of this room.
Do you think the people watching you at work are also aware of your personal life outside of the warehouse?

Okay. That's it. I'm done. I am literally sitting here, looking right at you, and you are asking me—again—about my personal life outside the warehouse! What did I just say? What did I just spend the last twenty minutes explaining to you? I swear, it's like talking to a brick wall. A highly paid brick wall with a notepad! 

I don't know how many different ways I can say the exact same thing before it actually clicks in your brain. Do they care about my personal life? No! They don't care if I go home and stare at the ceiling, they don't care what I buy at the grocery store, they don't care what color socks I wear on my day off! The only reason my personal life is even involved in this mess is because they dragged my husband into it to get what they want at work. They know him, they've seen him in the parking lot when he picks me up from my shifts, and they figured out that if they can get to him, they can get to me. 

Listen to me, and please, for the love of everything, actually hear the words I am saying. I came in here today because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy. That is it. That is the whole story. My husband is sitting at home right now looking at me like I'm a stranger because those guys at work played him like a fiddle. But I am not crazy. I know what they are doing. I know they have been watching my moves on the floor, tracking every single thing I do. I know they are changing the pallet counts in the system to ruin my numbers and make me look like a lazy worker. 

And they are doing all of this—every single bit of it—to keep me from getting that supervisor spot! 

That is all they care about! The supervisor spot! It means more money, it means I don't have to break my back lifting heavy freight and breathing in warehouse dust for ten hours a day. They want it for themselves, and they know I'm the one who actually earned it. So they mess with my counts, they watch my every move on the floor, and they tell my husband I'm losing my mind so I end up sitting in a psychiatrist's office instead of getting promoted. 

They don't care about my personal life, Doc. They care about the warehouse. Now, are you going to ask me something actually useful, or should I just get up and walk out that door right now? Because I am not doing this in circles with you anymore.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your coworkers might not be watching you or sabotaging your work?

Considered the possibility? Are you... wow. Just wow. You really just do not get it, do you? 

Do you think I haven't sat there in the breakroom, drinking a lukewarm coffee, staring at the concrete wall and wondering for just one second if maybe I am losing it? Of course I have! Because that is exactly what they are trying to make me think! They want me second-guessing myself. 

But then I go back out on the floor, and the proof is right there in my face. I am not stupid, Doc. I might not have a fancy college degree like you, but I know how to count. I know how much freight I move. Take last Tuesday, for example. I pulled, stacked, and shrink-wrapped forty-two pallets before lunch. Forty-two! My hands were covered in blisters from the tape dispenser, my shoulders were absolutely screaming from lifting heavy boxes of laundry detergent and dog food all morning. I know what I did. And then I check the system at the end of the shift, and what does it say? Twenty-eight. 

Twenty-eight! Where did the other fourteen pallets go? Did they just magically evaporate into the warehouse dust? No! 

So no, I don't consider the possibility that they aren't sabotaging me, because I have the math to prove it. I came in here today—and I know I sound like a broken record, but I have to keep saying it because you keep acting like it's some big mystery—I came in here because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy. They sit there and tell me, "Oh, you just miscounted," or "Oh, you're just stressed out from the long hours." My own husband looks at me like I need to be locked away somewhere! He actually believes them over his own wife!

But I am not crazy. I know they have been watching my moves. I see them ducking back behind the racking when I turn around in the aisle. I know they are logging in and changing the pallet counts to make my productivity look like complete trash. 

And why? Why do they do it? Because of the supervisor spot! If my numbers are garbage, management won't promote me. If they convince my husband I'm crazy and he makes me come to a psychiatrist, management definitely won't promote me. It is a setup, from start to finish, just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot so one of those lazy guys can take it and sit in the air-conditioned office while I stay out on the floor breaking my back. 

So don't sit there in your nice comfortable chair and ask me if I've "considered" that it isn't happening. It is happening. I live it every single day. Now, are you going to actually help me figure out how to deal with the stress of this, or are you just going to keep calling me a liar?
Can anything or anyone change your mind about people watching you and sabotaging your work at the warehouse?

Change my mind? Change my mind?! What is there to change, Doc? It’s not an opinion! It’s not like I’m sitting here deciding what my favorite color is and you can talk me into liking blue instead of red! You can't change someone's mind about something that is a cold, hard fact happening right in front of their face. 

I mean, I feel like I'm on trial here, and you're just not getting it. I have said this over and over until I'm blue in the face. I only came in here because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy. That is it. That is the whole entire reason I am wasting my afternoon in this office instead of picking up an extra shift. They treat me like I've completely lost it, but I know they have been watching my moves out there on the floor. I know they are changing the pallet counts. And I know exactly why they're doing it—to keep me from getting that supervisor spot! 

You want to know what would "change my mind"? If somebody could actually explain to me how my physical labor just vanishes into thin air! Show me the real system logs. Not the ones they doctored, the real ones. Show me the security cameras from aisle four that they probably delete the footage from every night. Because until somebody can do that, I know what my own two hands did. I know how much shrink wrap I went through. You don't just use three whole rolls of heavy-duty wrap on twenty-eight pallets. It takes way more than that for forty-two! I'm the one lifting those boxes of dog food, I'm the one sweating through my shirt by 9 AM, pulling the jack, feeling it in my lower back every single time I bend down. 

So don't ask me what's going to "change my mind" about my own reality. Nothing is going to change my mind because I am the one living it! They just want that promotion, and they figured out the easiest way to get me out of the running was to get in my husband's ear, make him think I'm a basket case, and have him drag me to a doctor so I look unstable to management. It's a game to them. But I'm not playing, and I'm definitely not changing my mind just because you all want me to.
Is there anything that could ever make you think that your coworkers are not watching you or sabotaging your work?

Are you... did you seriously just ask me the exact same thing again? I literally just answered that. Did you not hear me? Is your pen out of ink? I feel like I am losing my mind in this room with you, and I am not the crazy one here! 

I have told you, over and over, I came in here because my husband and the warehouse people keep acting like I'm crazy. That is the only reason I am sitting in this chair right now, losing out on my hourly wages, instead of being on the clock. And you just keep spinning me around in circles asking the same thing! 

I am not going to sit here and pretend that my reality isn't happening just to make you or my husband or those lazy guys at work feel better. I know they have been watching my moves on the floor. I know it. I see them out of the corner of my eye when I'm down in aisle four, I hear them whispering by the time clock when I walk past. I know they are logging into the computer system and changing the pallet counts to make my numbers look like garbage. 

And I know exactly why they are doing it, too. They are doing it to keep me from getting that supervisor spot! That is the entire point of this whole miserable situation! 

So what could make me think they aren't sabotaging me? Nothing! Because they are! What do you want me to do, just lie to you? Do you want me to sit here and say oh wow doctor, you are so right, maybe the warehouse fairies came down and magically un-stacked all those heavy boxes of dog food and laundry soap I broke my back lifting all morning? I am not going to say that! I am a hard worker. I don't have a high school diploma, I don't have a fancy office, but I have my work ethic, and they are trying to steal it from me so they can get the promotion and sit in the air conditioning while I rot on the floor. 

So no. Nothing will make me think otherwise. Are you going to actually write that down this time, or are you going to ask me the same exact question a fourth time? Because I can keep explaining it all day if I have to.
Is there anything that could make you doubt your belief that your coworkers are watching you and sabotaging your work?
